Kruze's checklist marks the detailed cap table, the option pool details, the funding history and the list of current investors as expected at every stage from pre-seed to Series C (a vendor view). The rows are in kruze_stage_rows.csv.

An SVB article reports that investors tend to prefer evenly split founder equity, and that a lopsided split such as 80-20 raises questions. It also passes on one entrepreneur's advice not to repay a founder for early expenses with equity; an IOU is cleaner.

BetaKit's investor Q&A says a broken ownership structure can discourage investors before they answer a data room, and shows ideal cap tables by stage that it says can vary by plus or minus 10 percent.

Colligan Law, a startup law firm, lists three repeat problems: dead equity, non-accredited investors in early rounds, and promises of a fixed ownership percentage or anti-dilution rights to early participants who add little.

A Hacker News commenter on the Stability AI co-founder story argues that 15 percent of zombie equity on the cap table would have made a large raise hard. It is one reader's view, not an investor's statement.

Kruze's checklist marks existing shareholder agreements, SAFE and convertible debt documentation, and the history of funding rounds with valuation and terms as expected at every stage (a vendor view). The rows are in kruze_stage_rows.csv.

The YC post-money SAFE guide says the pro rata right moved out of the standard SAFE into an optional side letter that applies to the round in which the SAFE converts, because the right is best handled case by case.

The YC SAFE guide's table says the post-money SAFE's Company Capitalization includes outstanding shares, outstanding options, promised options, the unissued option pool, and other SAFEs and convertibles, and leaves out an option pool increase made in the new round.
OneGC (a legal services vendor) says an acquisition before conversion lets a standard SAFE holder take the greater of the money back or the as-converted amount at the cap.
Allied Ventures (an investor network) says notes with maturity dates of 18 to 36 months act as deadlines, and that at maturity a note converts, is repaid with accrued interest, or is renegotiated.
Kruze's checklist asks for the last two 409A valuations and marks them No at pre-seed, Maybe at seed, and Yes from Series A on (a vendor view). The row is in kruze_stage_rows.csv.
Redwood Valuation (a valuation vendor) says a SAFE or note needs a case-by-case review as a refresh trigger: a small SAFE may not matter, but several closings totaling millions may.
CRV's guide says 409A providers and cap table platforms differ: platforms are faster and fine for simple cap tables, and a standalone firm fits better as Series A brings several preferred classes.

Kruze's checklist expects the articles of incorporation and the bylaws at every stage, and a state certificate of good standing as No at pre-seed and seed, Maybe at Series A and Series B, and Yes at Series C (a vendor view). The rows are in kruze_stage_rows.csv.

Holloway's guide (written by two lawyers) lists the formation set an investor should see: the certificate or articles, bylaws, the organizational consent of the initial directors, the incorporator's consent, a stock purchase agreement for each holder who subscribed, an IP assignment for each founder, the equity plan if there is one, and copies of filed 83(b) elections where founder shares vest.
The terms.law conversion guide says VCs will require a C-Corp before investing, so an LLC should convert before fundraising talks start (a legal services site).

Kruze's checklist asks for board and shareholder meeting minutes for the last three years, and marks them No at pre-seed and seed, Maybe at Series A, and Yes at Series B and C (a vendor view). The row is in kruze_stage_rows.csv.

A Delaware startup lawyer's article in the Orange County Business Journal (Rutan & Tucker) says shares found to be improperly issued are often discovered in a financing, that old ratification attempts did not work under Delaware case law, and that the 2014 statutory fix needs board action, sometimes stockholder approval, notice to all holders, and in some cases a certificate of validation with a filing fee.

Richards, Layton & Finger (a Delaware firm) reports that in Nguyen v. View the Court of Chancery held that a financing a founder had refused to approve could not be fixed by statutory ratification, because a no vote is not a failure of authorization.

Kruze's checklist asks for signed invention agreements from employees, founders and consultants since inception (Maybe at pre-seed and seed, Yes from Series A), and a list of people who have not signed (No at pre-seed, Maybe at seed, Yes from Series A) (a vendor view). The rows are in kruze_stage_rows.csv.

OneGC (a legal services vendor) says California Labor Code Section 2870 bars employers from requiring assignment of inventions an employee develops entirely on their own time, without company resources, and unrelated to the business, and that a PIIA ignoring state carve-outs may be partly unenforceable.

Cooley GO's glossary says a confidential information and inventions assignment agreement assigns IP an employee creates on the job to the employer and carves out IP created before the job. It also says such agreements often add nondisclosure and nonsolicitation terms, and that noncompetition clauses are unenforceable in some states such as California.

Kruze's checklist asks for a list of ongoing or potential legal disputes (Maybe at pre-seed, Yes from seed on), an overview of regulatory compliance (Maybe through Series A, Yes at Series B and C), and any pending or potential IP litigation (Maybe at pre-seed and seed, Yes from Series A) (a vendor view). The rows are in kruze_stage_rows.csv.

BCLP, a law firm, reports that in December 2024 the SEC settled actions against a private fund adviser and two pre-IPO companies for filing Form D late, which shows that a missed filing is a regulatory exposure for private issuers.

CourtListener's API documentation says authenticated users get a default of 5 requests per minute, 50 per hour and 125 per day, so a search for a company's federal dockets is rate limited unless the operator has a membership.

Promise Legal, a startup legal services site, says investors who cannot judge a startup's data practices tend to respond by lowering the valuation or SAFE cap, slowing the close, and asking for heavier disclosure schedules.

Venture Hacks (Nivi) publishes the Series A share-price formulas: new options n = (x times o times t) divided by (p minus o times t), share price s = p divided by (x plus n), and effective valuation e = s times x, where p is the pre-money, t the post-money, o the post-money pool share and x the existing shares.

Promise Legal (a legal services vendor) says diligence starts from cap table exports but tests them against documents, and that a table is compliant when its math matches the signed transaction documents and the company's corporate authority.
NASPP says an early-stage company might set aside 10 to 20 percent for an employee option pool, and that a pool that is missing or already used up could point to hiring and retention trouble.
LTSE says honest small mistakes such as wrong shareholder details are far more acceptable and less embarrassing than impossible entries.
Holloway tells the investor to make sure anyone who has already left signed an IP assignment agreement.

A VC newsletter (1752vc) says a founder with too little equity is a flight risk, a round made of many small checks with no lead can mean the smart money passed, and an early investor holding 30 to 40 percent can block the next round.
Cooley GO says it does not endorse its documents as a market standard and tells readers to have a lawyer check them.
CRV says pro rata rights are commonly limited to the largest check-writers and to the next round only.
CRV says that when a SAFE has both a cap and a discount, the investor gets the lower conversion price.

OneGC says that since 2023 a down or flat round against old caps is the scenario reshaping seed-stage cap tables, and that the lead may then ask for a bigger pool, tougher preferences or a smaller check.

The YC guide gives the pro rata formula: Safe Pro Rata Allocation % = Series A New Investors % divided by (100% minus Safes with Pro Rata %), minus Series A New Investors %. Its example comes to 4.41%.
BCLP, a law firm, reports that in December 2024 the SEC settled actions against a private fund adviser and two pre-IPO companies for filing Form D late.
Redwood says an appraiser typically asks for at least three years of financial statements, updated projections and a summary of significant business developments.
CRV says many companies complete their first 409A around their initial financing event, whether a note, a SAFE or a priced round.

CRV lists four common mistakes: waiting too long for the first valuation, using an outdated valuation after a funding event, confusing the 409A with the preferred valuation, and treating the process as a checkbox.

A Rutan & Tucker lawyer writes that Delaware startups often find improperly issued shares during an equity financing, that earlier ratification attempts failed under case law, and that a statute amended several years before 2017 now permits a cure.

A North Carolina Bar blog case study, built on a hypothetical startup, walks through a company that issued stock before electing a board and had to find and ratify each resulting defect, including an overissue.
Startups.com says amending the charter for more shares takes board approval, stockholder approval and a filing with the Secretary of State.
Rho (a banking vendor) says Delaware franchise tax is due each March 1 and that a late payment brings a $200 penalty plus 1.5% interest a month.
Cooley GO names a seed round financing, an additional credit line and an IPO as moments when evidence of board approval is requested.
a16z says minutes tend to be heavily redacted, and that it usually looks at board decks if they are available.

A North Carolina Bar blog case study, built on a hypothetical startup, lists several linked defects: no initial directors elected, an issuance without board authorization, a defective charter amendment and a defective director appointment.

A Rutan & Tucker lawyer writes that when stockholders would have needed to approve the original act, they must also ratify it, only holders of validly issued stock may vote on the ratification, and notice goes to all holders.
Cooley GO says the secretary of a meeting writes the minutes, the board approves them at a later meeting, and they are then signed and placed in the minute book.
CRV says piecemeal sharing of problems reads as a behavioral red flag.

OneGC says every priced-round term sheet includes a representation that the company owns or has valid licenses to all IP used in its business, and that if it cannot be made the deal is delayed, or if it is made and wrong it creates an indemnification liability.
OneGC calls missing assignment for pre-incorporation work the most common gap, and says the fix is a founder assignment signed at incorporation.
OneGC says copyleft licenses (GPL, AGPL, LGPL) in a product can require releasing proprietary code under the same license.

Wilson says a founder should ideally begin working on a startup after ending all previous employment, and should document that no work used the former employer's time, tools, customer lists or confidential information.
Weintraub's account says the developer demanded both compensation and equity before signing, and the founders lost months of momentum, valuation leverage and part of their cap table.
Cooley GO's request list also asks for licenses and agreements about the company's or others' patent, copyright, trade secret or other proprietary rights.
Cooley GO says the company almost always prepares the first draft of the disclosure schedule, because outside counsel does not see day-to-day operations.
REVERA says an investor will assess how material a dispute is, what it means for the investor, and how realistic it is to resolve before or after the deal.
CRV lists disclosure in pieces among data room mistakes and says piecemeal sharing reads as a behavioral red flag.
